place.rowan_grove.name: the rowan wood
quest.waxwing.title: A Waxwing for Sorokin
quest.waxwing.desc: A retired ornithologist lives in the Academgorodok. They say he knows everything about the birds here.
quest.waxwing.find.log: Sorokin is the one to ask about birds. He is a retired ornithologist and lives in the Academgorodok. He gets up before dawn, takes the morning train to the island to watch birds and comes back towards evening.
quest.waxwing.talk_sorokin.obj: Find Sorokin the ornithologist and talk to him
quest.waxwing.prepare.log: Sorokin said: the guide first, then the feed. The guide is in the Academgorodok's library; the Gastronom sells dried rowan and a feeder. He studied waxwings for forty years and has not seen one here: they keep to the old forest beyond the northern hills, and he can't walk that far any more. I'll go.
quest.waxwing.get_guide.obj: Take the bird guide from the library
quest.waxwing.get_rowan.obj: Buy dried rowan at the Gastronom
quest.waxwing.get_feeder.obj: Buy a bird feeder at the Gastronom
quest.waxwing.journey.log: I have everything. The waxwings live far to the north: across the whole town and on, in the old forest on the hills, where the rowans are. It is a long walk.
quest.waxwing.reach_grove.obj: Walk to the old forest beyond the northern hills
quest.waxwing.lure.log: This is the forest. There are rowans at every step. I should put the feeder up on level open ground and pour dried rowan into it.
quest.waxwing.fill_feeder.obj: Put the feeder up in the forest and fill it with rowan
quest.waxwing.wait.log: The feeder is up. Sorokin said birds find the feed in an hour and a half or two, and only by day: towards evening they are already off to roost. Step back twenty paces, crouch and keep still.
quest.waxwing.see_waxwing.obj: Wait by the feeder until a waxwing comes
quest.waxwing.tame.log: They have come. A crest, a yellow band on the tail, red drops on the wings. Now creep up quite slowly, crouching, and hold out a palm with rowan. No hurry.
quest.waxwing.tame_waxwing.obj: Feed a waxwing from the palm
quest.waxwing.return.log: I am a waxwing. Sorokin wanted to see just one. By day he is on the island or at home in the Academgorodok; at night he sleeps. Find him, come down beside him and call.
quest.waxwing.call_sorokin.obj: As the waxwing, find Sorokin, land beside him and call (F)
quest.waxwing.done: He knew me. Not me, of course. The waxwing. Forty years he went after them, and this one came by itself.
quest.waxwing_after.title: What Sorokin Saw
quest.waxwing_after.desc: A waxwing came to Sorokin. I wonder what he will say about it.
quest.waxwing_after.visit.log: I should drop in on Sorokin as a person now. And say nothing.
quest.waxwing_after.done: Sorokin entered the waxwing in his field journal and gave me feed from his own stock. Not a word about me in the journal. As it should be.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_meet.1: You're here about birds? Then you've come to the right man. Sorokin, ornithologist. Retired, but the birds don't know that.
line.hero.waxwing_meet.2: They eat from the hand here. Is that normal?
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_meet.3: It happens, if you don't hurry. But first learn to tell them apart. My guide is in the library; ask Olya.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_meet.4: And buy proper feed. The Gastronom has everything, from grain to dried rowan. The seeds from the vending machine are only good for pigeons.
line.hero.waxwing_meet.5: And which birds did you study?
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_meet.6: Waxwings. Forty years. A crest, red drops on the wings, a voice like a little silver bell.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_meet.7: And here I haven't seen a single one. They keep to the old forest beyond the northern hills, where the rowans are. I can't walk that far any more: my knees.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_meet.9: An hour's walk north, across the whole town and beyond. Without rowan and a feeder a waxwing won't come near you. It is a careful bird.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_tips.1: The guide is in the library, the rowan and the feeder at the Gastronom, the waxwings in the north beyond the hills. Don't mix them up.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_wait.1: Put the feeder in the open, but near trees. Fill it, step back, crouch. And wait. A bird tests a person with time.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_back.1: You look like someone who is up to something. Don't tell me. I only like surprises from birds.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_seen.2: A waxwing. Here. It came by itself.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_seen.3: Forty years I went after you. Well, hello.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_again.1: You again. Sit closer, I don't bite.
line.sorokin_oleg.bird_over.1: Who is that calling? Come down, show yourself. I haven't got my binoculars.
line.sorokin_oleg.bird_visit.1: Hello, hello. Not a waxwing, but good all the same.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_after.1: A waxwing came to me. It sat down beside me and called. To me, straight to me.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_after.3: Forty years I went after them, and this one came by itself. That isn't luck, young man. That is courtesy.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_after.4: Take these. Mealworms and peanuts, from my own stock. You need them more than I do.
line.sorokin_oleg.waxwing_journal.1: I entered it in the journal. Waxwing, one, adult. Under “behaviour” I wrote: said hello.
line.girl_b.waxwing_guide.1: The bird guide? Sorokin sent you, didn't he? There it is, on my desk.
line.girl_b.waxwing_guide.2: Just take it. He wrote it himself and told me to give it to anyone who asks about birds.
line.orlova_tanya.waxwing_rowan.1: Dried rowan? Only Sorokin ever bought it. He kept waiting for his waxwings.
line.orlova_tanya.waxwing_rowan.2: There's a feeder too. Without one the thrushes will carry your rowan off before you can blink.
